ops.text: Done is not landed: a run that ends done is finished only when gh pr view reads MERGED and origin/main moved, and it lands with npm run land:pr -- <n>, never a bare gh pr merge. MERGED (N commits) is a receipt for work already landed. After a restart, prove the served version changed.

Landing follows the remote: a GitHub repo lands with gh pr merge --rebase --admin; a SEFL Bitbucket repo by one turnover branch, worker branches rolled back locally and only that branch pushed. The LANDING block outranks the brief, and a refs-only task produces no commit and no PR.

Read live state from /api/jobs, never logs/jobs.json: a row is in flight only with a running job for its run id or its tree, never by its thread name, and a MESSAGE line is a request until the job store shows the turn it should have started.

A quiet npm test proves nothing, and a live --test child counts only when its start time matches the launch. An approval /api/approvals does not list is not a card, a 600-second expiry re-asked every ~10 minutes is a loop, and a watchdog naming a run that already ended is stale.

Never cut a worktree to compare, export or clean up: use git archive or git show. A RELEASE line is a request for the worker's own tree only - proof it is done, never that the tree is gone. A throwaway load generator binds 127.0.0.1, is time-limited and is torn down in the same run.

A parked row is a hold: it cannot be spawned, is not released by its blocker landing, and a sweep naming only parked rows reports a clean queue. Before spawning, check for a merged PR on the same files; finish one with a TO to the thread that owns the branch.

Judge a failed row by outcome.reason and its tree, never by the status word: max_turns means the turns ran out mid-task, so look for committed work owed a push and a PR. A run of patches to one file is not a loop while node --check passes and each new symbol appears once.

Every worker brief names the test files that cover the change and forbids the full suite; a full-suite run with no result after 20 minutes is cancelled. This checkout is CRLF with LF blobs, so a worker preserves the endings and proves byte identity against the blob, not the working copy.

Never push the oauth2-multi turnover branch 20260710_1338_DMR-39015_authorizationCodeFlowPCKE for any task: its history carries a real JWT private key in 25 commits plus a named OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET_VALUE, so a push publishes key material even when the tip tree is clean.
Never write U+2014 or U+2013 anywhere - replies, commits, PR titles and bodies, comments, docs, logs or shell output. Use a plain ASCII hyphen; those characters become mojibake under cp1252.
Outside oauth2-multi, a tree cut from a non-landing branch still lands by PR against the landing branch, merged with gh pr merge --rebase --admin; the LANDING header names the source, not the target.
